blocks.x: To test whether administrative propositions hold across cultures — and to avoid transplanting systems that will not take root.
blocks.th: **Wilson (1887)** urged comparison while warning against importing foreign systems; **Dahl (1947)** made it a condition of any science of administration.
blocks.in: Why Westminster forms sit on a colonial steel frame here.
blocks.gl: CAG group of the American Society for Public Administration, 1960s.

blocks.x: Societies move from **fused** (undifferentiated roles) through **prismatic** (transitional) to **diffracted** (specialised).
blocks.th: **Fred Riggs**; the **sala** is the prismatic office — part bureau, part household.
blocks.in: Merit rules coexisting with caste and kinship claims inside one office.
blocks.w: India is prismatic — which is why a rule can be **enacted, publicised and then not applied**.

blocks.x: **Heterogeneity** (modern and traditional side by side), **formalism** (gap between prescribed and practised), **overlapping** (formal structures performing informal functions).
blocks.th: **Riggs**; the bazaar-canteen economy and poly-communalism complete the picture.
blocks.in: Citizens' charters without remedies; social audit without independent auditors.
blocks.w: **Formalism** is the single most useful Riggsian term in an Indian answer.

blocks.x: Too pessimistic, static and derived from a Western ideal type; it describes dysfunction without a path out.
blocks.th: Critics within CAG; later development administration scholarship.
blocks.in: India's DPI and delivery successes sit awkwardly with the prismatic prediction.
blocks.gl: East Asian states that diffracted rapidly.
blocks.w: Use Riggs as a **diagnostic vocabulary**, not as a prophecy.

blocks.x: **UK** generalist and anonymous; **US** position-classified with a political appointee layer; **France** grands corps trained at ENA (now INSP); **China** cadre system under party supervision.
blocks.in: India blends the British model with **constitutional protection (Article 311)** and a **federal all-India service**.
blocks.gl: Senior Executive Service in the US.
blocks.w: India's distinctiveness is the **all-India service**, which no other federation has.

blocks.x: **Anglo-Saxon** — parliamentary, generalist; **Continental** — legalistic, prefectoral, administrative courts; **Soviet/Chinese** — party-supervised.
blocks.in: The Collector resembles a prefect more than a British civil servant.
blocks.w: India inherited a **prefectoral field system inside a parliamentary shell**.

blocks.x: Often the **most modern institution** in a traditional society, which gives it disproportionate power and invites over-bureaucratisation.
blocks.th: **Riggs's** warning about the bureaucratic elite outrunning political institutions.
blocks.in: Strong permanent executive alongside weak local political capacity.
blocks.w: Where politics is weak, **administration fills the vacuum** — and that is a democratic problem.

blocks.x: States now administer under external constraints — trade rules, treaty obligations, capital mobility, rating agencies.
blocks.in: WTO obligations shaping agricultural policy; FATF evaluation shaping PMLA enforcement.
blocks.w: Sovereignty is now exercised **within a web of obligations**, not above them.
